steps.title: France and beyond
steps.body: Cinsault grows across the Languedoc, Provence and the southern Rhône, mainly as a blending grape and in rosé. It was widely planted in Algeria and Morocco, and Lebanon's Bekaa Valley uses it, notably at Château Musar. South Africa and Chile's Itata Valley have old plantings.

steps.title: In blends
steps.body: In Châteauneuf-du-Pape and Côtes du Rhône, Cinsault adds perfume and softness to Grenache and Syrah. In the Languedoc, it softens Carignan. Its low tannin and freshness make blends more approachable. It's one of 13 grapes allowed in Châteauneuf.

steps.prompt: Match each place to its Cinsault.
steps.explanation: Cinsault spread around the Mediterranean and beyond.

steps.body: Chile's Itata Valley has old, dry-farmed Cinsault vines planted long ago. Young producers there now make light, fresh, affordable reds from them.
